units.zh: 唐有鹽池十八，井六百四十，皆隸度支。
units.en: Under the Tang there were eighteen salt ponds and six hundred forty salt wells, all administered by the Department of Expenditure.
units.literal: The Tang had eighteen salt ponds and six hundred forty wells; all were subordinate to the Department of Expenditure.

units.zh: 蒲州安邑、解縣有池五，總曰「兩池」，歲得鹽萬斛，以供京師。
units.en: In Puzhou, Anyi and Jie counties together had five ponds known as the "Two Ponds," which produced ten thousand hu of salt a year for the capital.
units.literal: At Anyi and Jie counties in Puzhou there were five ponds, together called the "Two Ponds"; each year they yielded ten thousand hu of salt to supply the capital.

units.zh: 鹽州五原有烏池、白池、瓦池、細項池，靈州有溫泉池、兩井池、長尾池、五泉池、紅桃池、回樂池、弘靜池、會州有河池，三州皆輸米以代鹽。
units.en: Yanzhou's Wuyuan had the Wu, Bai, Wa, and Xixiang ponds; Lingzhou had the Wenquan, Liangjing, Changwei, Wuquan, Hongtao, Huile, and Hongjing ponds; Huizhou had the He pond. These three prefectures all paid grain in place of salt tribute.
units.literal: At Wuyuan in Yanzhou were the Wu, Bai, Wa, and Xixiang ponds; at Lingzhou were the Wenquan, Liangjing, Changwei, Wuquan, Hongtao, Huile, and Hongjing ponds; at Huizhou was the He pond. All three prefectures paid grain in lieu of salt.

units.zh: 安北都護府有胡落池，歲得鹽萬四千斛，以給振武、天德。
units.en: The Anbei Protectorate had the Huluo salt pond, which yielded fourteen thousand hu a year to supply the Zhenwu and Tiande garrisons.
units.literal: The Protectorate General of the Pacified North had the Huluo pond, yielding fourteen thousand hu of salt yearly to supply Zhenwu and Tiande.

units.zh: 黔州有井四十一，成州、巂州井各一，果、閬、開、通井百二十三，山南西院領之。
units.en: Qianzhou had forty-one salt wells, Chengzhou and Xizhou one each, and Guo, Lang, Kai, and Tong one hundred twenty-three together—all under the Shannan West salt office.
units.literal: Qianzhou had forty-one wells; Chengzhou and Xizhou each had one; Guo, Lang, Kai, and Tong had one hundred twenty-three wells together, overseen by the Shannan West Circuit office.

units.zh: 邛、眉、嘉有井十三，劍南西川院領之。
units.en: Qiong, Mei, and Jia together had thirteen wells, administered by the Jiannan West salt office.
units.literal: Qiong, Mei, and Jia had thirteen wells, overseen by the Jiannan West Circuit office.

units.zh: 梓、遂、緜、合、昌、渝、瀘、資、榮、陵、簡有井四百六十，劍南東川院領之。
units.en: Zi, Sui, Mian, He, Chang, Yu, Lu, Zi, Rong, Ling, and Jian had four hundred sixty wells between them, under the Jiannan East salt office.
units.literal: Zi, Sui, Mian, He, Chang, Yu, Lu, Zi, Rong, Ling, and Jian had four hundred sixty wells, overseen by the Jiannan East Circuit office.

units.zh: 皆隨月督課。
units.en: Production at all of these sites was assessed and collected on a monthly schedule.
units.literal: All were supervised for production quotas month by month.

units.zh: 幽州、大同橫野軍有鹽屯，每屯有丁有兵，歲得鹽二千八百斛，下者千五百斛。
units.en: Youzhou and the Datong Hengye Army maintained salt colonies staffed by laborers and soldiers, with annual yields ranging from fifteen hundred to twenty-eight hundred hu.
units.literal: Youzhou and the Datong Hengye Army had salt colonies; each colony had laborers and troops, yielding twenty-eight hundred hu yearly at the top and fifteen hundred at the bottom.

units.zh: 負海州歲免租為鹽二萬斛以輸司農。
units.en: Coastal prefectures delivered twenty thousand hu of salt a year to the Court of Imperial Granaries in lieu of land tax.
units.literal: Coastal prefectures had their annual land tax remitted in return for delivering twenty thousand hu of salt to the Court of Imperial Granaries.

units.zh: 青、楚、海、滄、棣、杭、蘇等州，以鹽價市輕貨，亦輸司農。
units.en: Qing, Chu, Hai, Cang, Di, Hang, Su, and other prefectures used salt proceeds to buy light goods, which they also delivered to the Court of Imperial Granaries.
units.literal: Qing, Chu, Hai, Cang, Di, Hang, Su, and other prefectures used salt revenues to purchase light goods, which were also delivered to the Court of Imperial Granaries.

units.zh: 天寶、至德間，鹽每斗十錢。
units.en: From the Tianbao through the Zhide period, salt sold for ten cash a dou.
units.literal: Between the Tianbao and Zhide eras, salt was ten cash per dou.

units.zh: 乾元元年，鹽鐵、鑄錢使第五琦初變鹽法，就山海井竈近利之地置監院，游民業鹽者為亭戶，免雜傜。
units.en: In 758, Salt and Iron Commissioner Diwu Qi overhauled the salt law. He placed supervisory offices wherever mountains, coasts, wells, or salterns could profit, registered vagrant salt workers as saltern households, and exempted them from miscellaneous corvée.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, the Salt and Iron Commissioner and Mint Commissioner Diwu Qi first reformed the salt law: where mountains, seas, wells, and salterns offered profit, he set up supervisory offices; vagrants who worked salt became saltern households and were exempt from miscellaneous corvée.

units.zh: 盜鬻者論以法。
units.en: Anyone who stole and sold salt was prosecuted under the statute.
units.literal: Those who stole and sold salt were punished according to law.

units.zh: 及琦為諸州榷鹽鐵使，盡榷天下鹽，斗加時價百錢而出之，為錢一百一十。
units.en: Once Qi became commissioner for salt and iron monopolies across the prefectures, he brought all salt under state control, adding one hundred cash to the market price per dou and selling it for one hundred ten.
units.literal: When Qi became Commissioner for Monopolizing Salt and Iron in the Various Prefectures, he monopolized all salt under Heaven, adding one hundred cash to the current price per dou and selling it for one hundred ten cash.

units.zh: 自兵起，流庸未復，稅賦不足供費，鹽鐵使劉晏以為因民所急而稅之，則國足用。
units.en: After the rebellion began, refugees had not returned and tax income could not cover expenses. Salt Commissioner Liu Yan argued that levying taxes on what people could not do without would keep the state solvent.
units.literal: Since the armies rose, displaced persons had not returned and tax revenues were insufficient for expenses. The Salt and Iron Commissioner Liu Yan held that taxing what the people urgently need would suffice for state use.

units.zh: 於是上鹽法輕重之宜，以鹽吏多則州縣擾，出鹽鄉因舊監置吏，亭戶糶商人，縱其所之。
units.en: He then proposed a balanced salt policy: too many salt officials harassed local government. In producing districts he restored officers at existing posts, let saltern households sell to merchants, and allowed merchants to trade freely.
units.literal: Thereupon he presented what was fitting in the weight of the salt law: many salt officials disturbed prefectures and counties; in salt-producing districts he placed officers according to old supervisory posts; saltern households sold to merchants, who were allowed to go where they would.

units.zh: 江、嶺去鹽遠者，有常平鹽，每商人不至，則減價以糶民，官收厚利而人不知貴。
units.en: In the Yangzi and Ling regions far from salt sources he maintained Ever-Normal reserves: when merchants failed to arrive, officials cut prices to sell to the public. The state still took a large margin, yet consumers scarcely felt the burden.
units.literal: Where the Yangzi and Ling regions were far from salt, there was Ever-Normal salt; whenever merchants did not arrive, prices were reduced to sell to the people; the government took thick profit yet people did not feel it dear.

units.zh: 晏又以鹽生霖潦則鹵薄，暵旱則土溜墳，乃隨時為令，遣吏曉導，倍於勸農。
units.en: Yan also knew that heavy rains thinned the brine and droughts washed soil over the beds, so he issued seasonal orders and sent officers to guide production—more diligently than any agricultural campaign.
units.literal: Yan also held that when rain and flood came, brine grew thin, and when drought came, earth washed and mounded; he therefore issued timely orders and sent officers to instruct, with effort twice that of encouraging agriculture.

units.zh: 吳、越、揚、楚鹽廩至數千，積鹽二萬餘石。
units.en: Salt granaries in Wu, Yue, Yang, and Chu numbered in the thousands and held more than twenty thousand shi in reserve.
units.literal: Wu, Yue, Yang, and Chu salt granaries reached several thousand, storing more than twenty thousand shi of salt.

units.zh: 有漣水、湖州、越州、杭州四場，嘉興、海陵、鹽城、新亭、臨平、蘭亭、永嘉、大昌、候官、富都十監，歲得錢百餘萬緡，以當百餘州之賦。
units.en: Four production fields operated at Lianshui, Huzhou, Yuezhou, and Hangzhou, and ten supervisory posts at Jiaxing, Hailing, Yancheng, Xinting, Linping, Lanting, Yongjia, Dachang, Houguan, and Fudu. Annual revenue exceeded one million strings—equivalent to taxes from more than a hundred prefectures.
units.literal: There were four fields at Lianshui, Huzhou, Yuezhou, and Hangzhou, and ten supervisory posts at Jiaxing, Hailing, Yancheng, Xinting, Linping, Lanting, Yongjia, Dachang, Houguan, and Fudu; yearly receipts exceeded one million strings, equaling the tax of more than one hundred prefectures.

units.zh: 自淮北置巡院十三，曰揚州、陳許、汴州、廬壽、白沙、淮西、甬橋、浙西、宋州、泗州、嶺南、兗鄆、鄭滑，捕私鹽者，姦盜為之衰息。
units.en: North of the Huai he established thirteen patrol offices—from Yangzhou to Zheng-Hua—to suppress smuggling, and illicit salt trade sharply declined.
units.literal: North of the Huai he set up thirteen patrol offices—Yangzhou, Chenxu, Bianzhou, Lushou, Baisha, Huaixi, Yongqiao, Zhexi, Songzhou, Sizhou, Lingnan, Yan-Yun, and Zheng-Hua—to seize private salt; illicit trade thereby declined.

units.zh: 然諸道加榷鹽錢，商人舟所過有稅。
units.en: Yet circuits still added monopoly surcharges, and merchants were taxed at every port their boats touched.
units.literal: Yet the various circuits added monopoly salt surcharges, and wherever merchants' boats passed there were taxes.

units.zh: 晏奏罷州縣率稅，禁堰埭邀以利者。
units.en: Yan petitioned to end ad hoc local levies and to forbid dam keepers from extorting travelers for passage fees.
units.literal: Yan memorialized to abolish prefectural and county levies in kind and to forbid dams and weirs from intercepting travelers for profit.

units.zh: 晏之始至也，鹽利歲纔四十萬緡，至大曆末，六百餘萬緡。
units.en: When Yan took office annual salt revenue was only four hundred thousand strings; by the end of the Dali era it exceeded six million.
units.literal: When Yan first arrived, salt profit was only four hundred thousand strings yearly; by the end of Dali it was more than six million.

units.zh: 天下之賦，鹽利居半，宮闈服御、軍饟、百官祿俸皆仰給焉。
units.en: Salt profits accounted for half of national revenue, funding palace supplies, army rations, and official salaries alike.
units.literal: Of all revenue under Heaven, salt profit comprised half; palace apparel, army provisions, and officials' salaries all depended on it.

units.zh: 明年而晏罷。
units.en: The following year Yan was removed from office.
units.literal: The next year Yan was dismissed.

units.zh: 貞元四年，淮南節度使陳少游奏加民賦，自此江淮鹽每斗亦增二百，為錢三百一十，其後復增六十，河中兩池鹽每斗為錢三百七十。
units.en: In 788 Huainan governor Chen Shaoyou petitioned to raise civilian taxes. Jiang-Huai salt then rose two hundred cash per dou to three hundred ten, later another sixty; salt from the Two Ponds in Hezhong sold for three hundred seventy a dou.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, the Huainan military governor Chen Shaoyou memorialized to increase the people's tax burden; from this the Jiang-Huai salt per dou also rose two hundred, making three hundred ten cash; later it rose again by sixty; the Two Ponds salt in Hezhong was three hundred seventy cash per dou.

units.zh: 江淮豪賈射利，或時倍之，官收不能過半，民始怨矣。
units.en: Wealthy Jiang-Huai merchants speculated, sometimes doubling prices, while the state captured less than half the proceeds—and popular resentment began.
units.literal: Jiang-Huai great merchants sought profit and at times doubled prices; the government could collect no more than half; the people began to resent it.

units.zh: 劉晏鹽法既成，商人納絹以代鹽利者，每緡加錢二百，以備將士春服。
units.en: After Liu Yan's salt reforms, merchants paying silk in lieu of salt dues paid an extra two hundred cash per string to fund spring uniforms for the troops.
units.literal: Once Liu Yan's salt law was established, merchants who paid silk in lieu of salt profit had two hundred cash added per string, to prepare spring uniforms for officers and soldiers.

units.zh: 包佶為汴東水陸運、兩稅、鹽鐵使，許以漆器、瑇瑁、綾綺代鹽價，雖不可用者亦高估而售之，廣虛數以罔上。
units.en: As transport, tax, and salt commissioner Bao Ji let merchants pay salt dues in lacquer, tortoiseshell, and brocade—even worthless goods at inflated prices—padding accounts to deceive the court.
units.literal: Bao Ji was Commissioner for Bian-East Water and Land Transport, the Two Taxes, and Salt and Iron; he allowed lacquerware, tortoiseshell, and fine silks to substitute for salt price; even unusable goods were overvalued and sold, inflating false figures to deceive the throne.

units.zh: 亭戶冒法，私鬻不絕，巡捕之卒，遍于州縣。
units.en: Saltern households broke the law and illicit sales continued unabated, while patrol troops spread through every prefecture and county.
units.literal: Saltern households violated the law; private sale did not cease; patrol soldiers were everywhere in prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 鹽估益貴，商人乘時射利，遠鄉貧民困高估，至有淡食者。
units.en: Salt prices kept rising as merchants profiteered. Poor villagers in remote districts, crushed by inflated valuations, were reduced to eating food without salt.
units.literal: Salt valuations grew ever dearer; merchants seized the moment for profit; poor people in distant districts were strained by high valuations, until some ate food without salt.

units.zh: 巡吏既多，官冗傷財，當時病之。
units.en: With so many patrol officers, bureaucratic bloat drained the treasury—a grievance widely noted at the time.
units.literal: Patrol officers being numerous, redundant officials harmed the treasury; contemporaries regarded this as a malady.

units.zh: 其後軍費日增，鹽價寖貴，有以穀數斗易鹽一升。
units.en: As military costs mounted, salt prices kept climbing until some people traded several dou of grain for a single sheng of salt.
units.literal: Afterward military expenses daily increased and salt prices gradually grew dear; some exchanged several dou of grain for one sheng of salt.

units.zh: 私糴犯法，未嘗少息。
units.en: Illegal private trade never let up.
units.literal: Private purchase in violation of law never for a moment ceased.

units.zh: 順宗時始減江淮鹽價，每斗為錢二百五十，河中兩池鹽，斗錢三百。
units.en: Under Emperor Shunzong Jiang-Huai salt was cut to two hundred fifty cash a dou, and the Two Ponds salt in Hezhong to three hundred.
units.literal: In the time of Shunzong Jiang-Huai salt prices were first reduced to two hundred fifty cash per dou; the Two Ponds salt in Hezhong was three hundred cash per dou.

units.zh: 增雲安、渙陽、塗𣉯三監。
units.en: Three new salt supervisory posts were established at Yun'an, Huanyang, and Tuwei.
units.literal: Three supervisory posts were added at Yun'an, Huanyang, and Tuwei.

units.zh: 其後鹽鐵使李錡奏江淮鹽斗減錢十以便民，未幾復舊。
units.en: Later Salt Commissioner Li Qi petitioned to cut Jiang-Huai salt by ten cash a dou to ease the burden on the people, but the reduction was soon reversed.
units.literal: Afterward the Salt and Iron Commissioner Li Qi memorialized to reduce Jiang-Huai salt by ten cash per dou for the people's convenience; before long the old price returned.

units.zh: 方是時，錡盛貢獻以固寵，朝廷大臣，皆餌以厚貨，鹽鐵之利，積于私室，而國用耗屈，榷鹽法大壞，多為虛估，率千錢不滿百三十而已。
units.en: Li Qi lavished tribute to secure favor and bribed senior ministers with rich gifts, hoarding salt profits privately while the treasury emptied. The monopoly system collapsed into sham valuations—of every thousand cash collected, barely one hundred thirty was real revenue.
units.literal: At that time Qi made lavish tribute to secure favor; court great ministers were all baited with rich goods; salt and iron profit accumulated in private chambers while state use was exhausted; the monopoly salt law was greatly ruined, mostly false valuations, so that per thousand cash not even one hundred thirty were real.

units.zh: 兵部侍郎李巽為使，以鹽利皆歸度支，物無虛估，天下糶鹽稅茶，其贏六百六十五萬緡。
units.en: When Vice Minister Li Xun took charge, salt revenue returned fully to the Department of Expenditure with no inflated valuations. Nationwide salt sales and tea taxes yielded a surplus of 6.65 million strings.
units.literal: Vice Minister of War Li Xun became commissioner; salt profit all returned to the Department of Expenditure; goods had no false valuation; selling salt and taxing tea under Heaven yielded a surplus of six million six hundred fifty thousand strings.

units.zh: 初歲之利，如劉晏之季年，其後則三倍晏時矣。
units.en: The first year's yield matched Liu Yan's final year; within a few years revenue tripled Yan's peak.
units.literal: The first year's profit matched Liu Yan's final years; afterward it was three times Yan's time.

units.zh: 兩池鹽利，歲收百五十餘萬緡。
units.en: The Two Ponds alone brought in more than 1.5 million strings a year.
units.literal: Profit from the Two Ponds yearly collected more than one million five hundred thousand strings.

units.zh: 四方豪商猾賈，雜處解縣，主以郎官，其佐貳皆御史。
units.en: Wealthy and unscrupulous merchants from every region gathered at Jie County, headed by a court gentleman with censors as deputies.
units.literal: Great merchants and crafty traders from the four directions mingled at Jie County; the chief was a court gentleman, and his assistants were all censors.

units.zh: 鹽民田園籍於縣，而令不得以縣民治之。
units.en: Although salt workers' land was registered locally, magistrates could not treat them as ordinary county subjects.
units.literal: Salt workers' fields and gardens were registered in the county, yet the magistrate could not govern them as county people.

units.zh: 憲宗之討淮西也，度支使皇甫鎛加劍南東西兩川、山南西道鹽估以供軍。
units.en: During Xianzong's campaign against Huaixi, Expenditure Commissioner Huangfu Bo raised salt valuations in eastern and western Jiannan and Shannan West to fund the war.
units.literal: When Xianzong campaigned against Huaixi, the Expenditure Commissioner Huangfu Bo raised salt valuations in the two Jiannan circuits east and west and the Shannan West circuit to supply the army.

units.zh: 貞元中，盜鬻兩池鹽一石者死，至元和中，減死流天德五城，鎛奏論死如初。
units.en: Under Zhenyuan, selling a shi of smuggled Two Ponds salt meant death; under Yuanhe the penalty was reduced to exile at the Five Forts of Tiande. Huangfu Bo petitioned to restore the death penalty.
units.literal: In Zhenyuan, selling one shi of stolen Two Ponds salt was death; by Yuanhe it was reduced to exile at the Five Forts of Tiande; Bo memorialized to restore death as before.

units.zh: 一斗以上杖背，沒其車驢，能捕斗鹽者賞千錢；
units.en: Offenders with a dou or more were flogged and their transport confiscated; anyone who seized a dou of smuggled salt received a thousand-cash reward;
units.literal: One dou or more was punished with back beating; cart and donkey were confiscated; one who could seize a dou of salt was rewarded one thousand cash;

units.zh: 節度觀察使以判官、州以司錄錄事參軍察私鹽，漏一石以上罰課料；
units.en: governors and observation commissioners assigned aides, and prefectures assigned clerks to police smuggling; officials who let a shi or more pass lost their salary allotments;
units.literal: military governors and observation commissioners used aides, and prefectures used clerks and recorders to inspect private salt; letting one shi or more slip was punished by withholding salary allotments;

units.zh: 鬻兩池鹽者，坊市居邸主人、市儈皆論坐；
units.en: anyone selling Two Ponds salt implicated innkeepers and brokers in the wards and markets;
units.literal: those who sold Two Ponds salt—ward and market lodging-house masters and brokers were all prosecuted;

units.zh: 盜刮鹻土一斗，比鹽一升。
units.en: stealing a dou of brine earth was punished as equivalent to a sheng of salt.
units.literal: stealing one dou of brine earth was equated to one sheng of salt.

units.zh: 州縣團保相察，比於貞元加酷矣。
units.en: Prefectures and counties organized mutual surveillance groups—harsher than the Zhenyuan regulations.
units.literal: Prefectures and counties formed mutual surveillance groups; compared with Zhenyuan it was harsher.

units.zh: 自兵興，河北鹽法羈縻而已。
units.en: After the rebellions began, Hebei salt policy was only loosely enforced.
units.literal: Since the armies rose, the Hebei salt law was only loosely controlled.

units.zh: 至皇甫鎛又奏置榷鹽使，如江淮榷法，犯禁歲多。
units.en: Huangfu Bo then petitioned to install salt monopoly commissioners on the Jiang-Huai model, and violations grew year by year.
units.literal: When Huangfu Bo again memorialized to set up salt monopoly commissioners like the Jiang-Huai monopoly law, violations yearly increased.

units.zh: 及田弘正舉魏博歸朝廷，穆宗命河北罷榷鹽。
units.en: When Tian Hongzheng returned Weibo to the throne, Emperor Muzong abolished the Hebei salt monopoly.
units.literal: When Tian Hongzheng brought Weibo back to the court, Muzong ordered Hebei to abolish the salt monopoly.

units.zh: 戶部侍郎張平叔議榷鹽法弊，請糶鹽可以富國，詔公卿議其可否。
units.en: Vice Minister Zhang Pingshu argued that monopoly salt policy was broken and that state salt sales could enrich the country. The emperor ordered senior ministers to debate the proposal.
units.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Pingshu discussed the defects of the salt monopoly law and requested that selling salt could enrich the state; an edict ordered the high ministers to debate whether it was feasible.

units.zh: 中書舍人韋處厚、兵部侍郎韓愈條詰之，以為不可，平叔屈服。
units.en: Secretariat Drafter Wei Chuhou and Vice Minister Han Yu rebutted the plan point by point as unworkable, and Pingshu backed down.
units.literal: Palace Drafting Attendant Wei Chuhou and Vice Minister of War Han Yu itemized objections and held it impossible; Pingshu yielded.

units.zh: 是時奉天鹵池生水柏，以灰一斛得鹽十二斤，利倍鹻鹵。
units.en: At Fengtian the brine ponds then yielded water cypress ash from which one hu produced twelve jin of salt—twice the profit of ordinary brine evaporation.
units.literal: At that time the Fengtian brine pond produced water cypress; from one hu of ash twelve jin of salt were obtained, profit doubling brine evaporation.

units.zh: 文宗時，采灰一斗，比鹽一斤論罪。
units.en: Under Wenzong, collecting a dou of ash was punished as equivalent to stealing a jin of salt.
units.literal: In the time of Wenzong, gathering one dou of ash was punished as equivalent to one jin of salt.

units.zh: 開成末，詔私鹽月再犯者，易縣令，罰刺史俸；
units.en: Late in the Kaicheng era an edict decreed that if smuggling recurred twice in a month, the county magistrate would be replaced and the prefect's salary docked;
units.literal: At the end of Kaicheng, an edict held that where private salt recurred twice in a month, the county magistrate was replaced and the prefect's salary was fined;

units.zh: 十犯，則罰觀察、判官課料。
units.en: after ten violations, the observation commissioner and his aide lost their salary allotments.
units.literal: at ten violations, the observation commissioner and aide had their salary allotments fined.

units.zh: 宣宗即位，茶、鹽之法益密，糶鹽少、私盜多者，讁觀察、判官，不計十犯。
units.en: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, tea and salt regulations tightened: commissioners and aides were censured whenever official sales lagged and smuggling flourished, with no ten-strike threshold.
units.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, tea and salt laws grew stricter; where official salt sales were few and private theft many, observation commissioners and aides were censured without counting ten violations.

units.zh: 戶部侍郎、判度支盧弘止以兩池鹽法敝，遣巡院官司空輿更立新法，其課倍入，遷榷鹽使。
units.en: Vice Minister Lu Hongzhi, finding the Two Ponds system failing, sent patrol official Sikong Yu to draft new rules. Revenue doubled, and Yu was promoted to Salt Monopoly Commissioner.
units.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Lu Hongzhi, because the Two Ponds salt law was worn out, sent patrol-office official Sikong Yu to establish a new law; revenue doubled and he was promoted Salt Monopoly Commissioner.

units.zh: 以壕籬者，鹽池之隄禁，有盜壞與鬻鹻皆死，鹽盜持弓矢者亦皆死刑。
units.en: Moats and fences guarded the pond dikes: damaging them or selling brine was capital, and salt smugglers armed with bows faced execution as well.
units.literal: By moat and fence were meant the dikes and prohibitions of the salt ponds; those who stole and damaged or sold brine were all put to death; salt thieves bearing bow and arrow were also all capital crimes.

units.zh: 兵部侍郎、判度支周墀又言：「兩池鹽盜販者，迹其居處，保、社按罪。
units.en: Vice Minister Zhou Chi also proposed: "For Two Ponds smugglers, trace their dwellings and hold mutual-aid groups and village communities collectively liable.
units.literal: Vice Minister of War and Acting Expenditure Commissioner Zhou Chi also said: "For Two Ponds salt smugglers, trace their dwellings; mutual-aid groups and village communities assign guilt.

units.zh: 鬻五石，市二石，亭戶盜糶二石，皆死。」
units.en: Selling five shi, buying two shi, or saltern households illicitly selling two shi—all carried the death penalty."
units.literal: Selling five shi, buying two shi, or saltern households secretly selling two shi—all were death."

units.zh: 是時江、吳羣盜，以所剽物易茶鹽，不受者焚其室廬，吏不敢枝梧，鎮戍、場鋪、堰埭以關通致富。
units.en: Meanwhile Jiang and Wu bandits traded loot for tea and salt, burning the homes of anyone who refused. Officials dared not resist, while garrison posts, depots, and toll dams grew rich controlling the routes.
units.literal: At that time Jiang and Wu bandits exchanged plunder for tea and salt; those who refused had their houses burned; officers dared not resist; garrison posts, depots, and dam passes grew rich on transit control.

units.zh: 宣宗乃擇嘗更兩畿輔望縣令者為監院官。
units.en: Xuanzong then appointed former magistrates of prestigious capital-region counties to supervise the salt offices.
units.literal: Xuanzong then chose men who had served as magistrates of renowned counties in the two capitals regions to be supervisory-office officers.

units.zh: 戶部侍郎裴休為鹽鐵使，上鹽法八事，其法皆施行，兩池榷課大增。
units.en: Vice Minister Pei Xiu became Salt Commissioner, submitted an eight-point salt reform, saw every measure enacted, and sharply increased Two Ponds monopoly revenue.
units.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Xiu became Salt and Iron Commissioner, presented eight items of salt law, all were put into effect, and Two Ponds monopoly revenue greatly increased.

units.zh: 其後兵遍天下，諸鎮擅利，兩池為河中節度使王重榮所有，歲貢鹽三千車。
units.en: Later, as warfare engulfed the empire, regional commands seized profits for themselves. Wang Chongrong, governor of Hezhong, controlled the Two Ponds and sent three thousand cartloads of salt in annual tribute.
units.literal: Afterward armies spread over all under Heaven; the various commands monopolized profit; the Two Ponds were held by the Hezhong military governor Wang Chongrong, who yearly presented three thousand cartloads of salt.

units.zh: 中官田令孜募新軍五十四都，餫轉不足，乃倡議兩池復歸鹽鐵使，而重榮不奉詔，至舉兵反，僖宗為再出，然而卒不能奪。
units.en: Eunuch Tian Lingzi raised fifty-four new army units but could not supply them. He urged returning the Two Ponds to the Salt and Iron Commissioner; Wang Chongrong refused, rebelled, and forced Emperor Xizong to flee the capital again, yet the court never regained the ponds.
units.literal: The eunuch Tian Lingzi raised fifty-four new army commands, but transport provisions were insufficient. He therefore proposed returning the Two Ponds to the Salt and Iron Commissioner. Chongrong refused the edict and went so far as to raise troops in rebellion, forcing Xizong to flee the capital a second time; even then, the court ultimately could not take the ponds from him.

units.zh: 唐初無酒禁。
units.en: Early in the Tang there was no prohibition on alcohol.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tang there was no ban on wine.

units.zh: 乾元元年，京師酒貴，肅宗以稟食方屈，乃禁京城酤酒，期以麥熟如初。
units.en: In 758 capital wine prices soared. Because grain rations were tight, Suzong banned wine sales in the capital until the wheat harvest.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan wine in the capital was dear; Suzong, because grain rations were strained, banned wine-selling in the capital, expecting to restore the former state when wheat ripened.

units.zh: 二年，饑，復禁酤，非光祿祭祀、燕蕃客，不御酒。
units.en: The next year famine returned and the ban was reimposed. The court served wine only for Guanglu sacrifices and banquets for foreign envoys.
units.literal: In the second year there was famine; the ban on selling was restored; except for Guanglu sacrifices and banquets for foreign guests, wine was not used at court.

units.zh: 廣德二年，定天下酤戶以月收稅。
units.en: In 764 the state required all licensed wine sellers to pay a monthly tax.
units.literal: In the second year of Guangde, wine-selling households under Heaven were fixed to pay tax monthly.

units.zh: 建中元年，罷之。
units.en: In 780 the levy was abolished.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong it was abolished.

units.zh: 三年，復禁民酤，以佐軍費，置肆釀酒，斛收直三千，州縣總領，醨薄私釀者論其罪。
units.en: Three years later private sales were banned again to fund the army. The state opened breweries charging three thousand cash per hu, with prefectures and counties in charge, and punished illegal home brewing.
units.literal: In the third year private selling was again banned to assist military expenses; shops were set up to brew wine, three thousand cash collected per hu; prefectures and counties oversaw it; those who brewed thin wine privately were punished by law.

units.zh: 尋以京師四方所湊，罷榷。
units.en: Soon afterward, because the capital drew goods from every direction, the monopoly was lifted.
units.literal: Soon, because the capital was where the four directions converged, the monopoly was abolished.

units.zh: 貞元二年，復禁京城、畿縣酒，天下置肆以酤者，斗錢百五十，免其傜役，獨淮南、忠武、宣武、河東榷麴而已。
units.en: In 786 wine was banned again in the capital and nearby counties. Licensed sellers nationwide paid one hundred fifty cash per dou and were exempt from corvée, while only Huainan, Zhongwu, Xuanwu, and Hedong retained yeast monopolies.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan wine was again banned in the capital and metropolitan counties; shops selling under Heaven paid one hundred fifty cash per dou and were exempt from corvée; only Huainan, Zhongwu, Xuanwu, and Hedong monopolized yeast mash.

units.zh: 元和六年，罷京師酤肆，以榷酒錢隨兩稅青苗斂之。
units.en: In 811 capital wine shops were closed and wine tax was folded into the two-tax and green-sprout assessments.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe capital wine shops were abolished; monopoly wine money was collected with the two taxes and green-sprout tax.

units.zh: 大和八年，遂罷京師榷酤。
units.en: In 834 the capital wine monopoly was finally abolished.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Dahe the capital wine monopoly was finally abolished.

units.zh: 凡天下榷酒為錢百五十六萬餘緡，而釀費居三之一，貧戶逃酤不在焉。
units.en: Nationwide wine monopoly revenue totaled 1.56 million strings, one third of which went to brewing costs—not counting poor households who evaded the tax.
units.literal: In all, wine monopoly under Heaven was one million five hundred sixty thousand strings, of which brewing costs were one third; poor households who evaded selling were not included.

units.zh: 昭宗世，以用度不足，易京畿近鎮麴法，復榷酒以贍軍，鳳翔節度使李茂貞方顓其利，按兵請入奏利害，天子遽罷之。
units.en: Under Zhaozong, the cash-strapped court altered yeast regulations near the capital and restored the wine monopoly to fund the army. Fengxiang Military Governor Li Maozhen, who had controlled the profits, held his troops in readiness and requested an audience to argue the policy's merits. The emperor immediately canceled it.
units.literal: In Zhaozong's reign, because expenditures were insufficient, the yeast regulations of the capital region and nearby commands were changed and the wine monopoly was restored to support the army. Fengxiang Military Governor Li Maozhen had been monopolizing the profits; he held his troops in readiness and requested permission to enter court to explain the policy's advantages and harms. The emperor hastily abolished it.

units.zh: 初，德宗納戶部侍郎趙贊議，稅天下茶、漆、竹、木，十取一，以為常平本錢。
units.en: Initially Dezong adopted Vice Minister Zhao Zan's plan to tax tea, lacquer, bamboo, and timber nationwide at ten percent to fund Ever-Normal Granary reserves.
units.literal: At first, Dezong accepted the proposal of Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Zan to tax tea, lacquer, bamboo, and wood under Heaven at one in ten, as capital for the Ever-Normal Granaries.

units.zh: 及出奉天，乃悼悔，下詔亟罷之。
units.en: After fleeing to Fengtian he repented and urgently abolished the levies by edict.
units.literal: When he went out to Fengtian he mourned and repented, and issued an edict urgently abolishing it.

units.zh: 及朱泚平，佞臣希意興利者益進。
units.en: After Zhu Ci's rebellion was crushed, ever more courtiers currying favor pushed profit-seeking schemes.
units.literal: When Zhu Ci was pacified, sycophants who sought profit by pleasing the ruler advanced ever more.

units.zh: 貞元八年，以水災減稅，明年，諸道鹽鐵使張滂奏：出茶州縣若山及商人要路，以三等定估，十稅其一。
units.en: In 792 flood relief cut taxes; the next year Circuit Salt Commissioner Zhang Pang proposed taxing tea at ten percent with three-tier valuations at producing counties, mountain districts, and major trade routes.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan taxes were reduced because of flood; the next year the Circuit Salt and Iron Commissioner Zhang Pang memorialized: set out tea-producing prefectures and counties, mountains, and merchants' key routes, fix valuations in three grades, and tax one in ten.

units.zh: 自是歲得錢四十萬緡，然水旱亦未嘗拯之也。
units.en: Thereafter the levy brought in four hundred thousand strings a year, yet none of it was ever used for flood or drought relief.
units.literal: From this yearly receipts were four hundred thousand strings, yet flood and drought were never relieved by it.

units.zh: 穆宗即位，兩鎮用兵，帑藏空虛，禁中起百尺樓，費不可勝計。
units.en: When Muzong ascended the throne, war on two fronts emptied the treasury while the palace built a hundred-foot tower at incalculable cost.
units.literal: When Muzong took the throne, two commands used troops; the treasury was empty; within the palace a hundred-foot tower was raised, expenses beyond counting.

units.zh: 鹽鐵使王播圖寵以自幸，乃增天下茶稅，率百錢增五十。
units.en: Salt Commissioner Wang Bo, courting imperial favor, raised the national tea tax by fifty percent—fifty cash on every hundred.
units.literal: The Salt and Iron Commissioner Wang Bo, seeking favor to secure himself, then increased tea tax under Heaven, generally adding fifty to every hundred cash.

units.zh: 江淮、浙東西、嶺南、福建、荊襄茶，播自領之，兩川以戶部領之。
units.en: Bo personally controlled tea in Jiang-Huai, eastern and western Zhe, Lingnan, Fujian, and Jing-Xiang, while the Ministry of Revenue handled the two Sichuan circuits.
units.literal: Tea of Jiang-Huai, Zhe east and west, Lingnan, Fujian, and Jing-Xiang Bo oversaw himself; the two Sichuan circuits were overseen by the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 天下茶加斤至二十兩，播又奏加取焉。
units.en: Nationwide, twenty liang were added to each jin of tea sold, and Bo petitioned for yet another surcharge.
units.literal: Tea under Heaven had weight added to each jin up to twenty liang; Bo again memorialized to add further collection.

units.zh: 右拾遺李珏上疏諫曰：「榷率起於養兵，今邊境無虞，而厚斂傷民，不可一也。
units.en: Right Reminder Li Jue submitted a memorial of protest: "Monopoly taxes were meant to fund armies. The borders are now peaceful, yet heavy levies still harm the people—that is the first objection.
units.literal: Right Reminder Li Jue memorialized in remonstrance: "Monopoly rates arose to support armies; now the borders are untroubled, yet heavy levies harm the people—this cannot be, first.

units.zh: 茗飲，人之所資，重稅則價必增，貧弱益困，不可二也。
units.en: Tea is a daily necessity. Heavy taxes must raise prices and further burden the poor—that is the second objection.
units.literal: Tea drinking is what people rely on; heavy tax then necessarily raises price, and the poor and weak are further strained—this cannot be, second.

units.zh: 山澤之饒，其出不訾，論稅以售多為利，價騰踊則市者稀，不可三也。」
units.en: Mountain and marsh yields are limitless in principle, yet taxing by volume sold for profit drives prices so high that buyers disappear—that is the third objection."
units.literal: The abundance of mountains and marshes, its output cannot be measured; taxing by volume sold for profit—when price soars buyers are few—this cannot be, third."

units.zh: 其後王涯判二使，置榷茶使，徙民茶樹於官場，焚其舊積者，天下大怨。
units.en: Later Wang Ya headed both commissions, created a Tea Monopoly Commissioner, transplanted private tea trees to government plantations, and burned existing stockpiles—provoking widespread outrage.
units.literal: Afterward Wang Ya judged the two commissions, set up a Tea Monopoly Commissioner, moved the people's tea trees to government fields, and burned their old stores; all under Heaven greatly resented it.

units.zh: 令狐楚代為鹽鐵使兼榷茶使，復令納榷，加價而已。
units.en: Linghu Chu succeeded him as Salt and Iron Commissioner and also Tea Monopoly Commissioner, restoring monopoly payments with price increases only.
units.literal: Linghu Chu replaced him as Salt and Iron Commissioner and also Tea Monopoly Commissioner, restoring payment of monopoly dues with price increase only.

units.zh: 李石為相，以茶稅皆歸鹽鐵，復貞元之制。
units.en: When Li Shi became chancellor, tea revenue returned to the Salt and Iron administration and the Zhenyuan system was restored.
units.literal: Li Shi became chancellor; tea tax all returned to Salt and Iron; the Zhenyuan system was restored.

units.zh: 武宗即位，鹽鐵轉運使崔珙又增江淮茶稅。
units.en: When Wuzong ascended the throne, Transport Commissioner Cui Gong raised Jiang-Huai tea taxes again.
units.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, the Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Cui Gong again increased Jiang-Huai tea tax.

units.zh: 是時茶商所過州縣有重稅，或掠奪舟車，露積雨中，諸道置邸以收稅，謂之「搨地錢」，故私販益起。
units.en: Tea merchants faced heavy taxes in every prefecture and county they passed, with boats sometimes seized and cargo left exposed in the rain. Circuits set up tax lodges charging what was called "ground-pressing money," and smuggling only increased.
units.literal: At that time wherever tea merchants passed, prefectures and counties had heavy taxes; sometimes boats and carts were plundered and goods lay exposed in rain; the various circuits set lodges to collect tax, called "ground-pressing money"; therefore private trade increased ever more.

units.zh: 大中初，鹽鐵轉運使裴休著條約：私鬻三犯皆三百斤，乃論死；
units.en: Early in the Dazhong era, Transport Commissioner Pei Xiu issued regulations: three convictions for selling three hundred jin of tea illegally meant death;
units.literal: Early in Dazhong, the Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Pei Xiu set forth regulations: private sale with three offenses each of three hundred jin was punished by death;

units.zh: 長行羣旅，茶雖少皆死；
units.en: itinerant merchant bands faced death for carrying even a small amount of tea;
units.literal: for itinerant merchant bands, possession of even a little tea meant death;

units.zh: 雇載三犯至五百斤、居舍儈保四犯至千斤者，皆死；
units.en: hired carriers convicted three times up to five hundred jin, and innkeepers and brokers four times up to one thousand jin, all faced execution;
units.literal: hired carriers with three offenses up to five hundred jin, lodging-house masters and brokers with four offenses up to one thousand jin—all were death;

units.zh: 園戶私鬻百斤以上，杖背，三犯，加重傜；
units.en: tea growers selling more than one hundred jin privately were flogged; after three offenses their corvée was doubled;
units.literal: estate households selling privately one hundred jin or more were flogged on the back; at three offenses, corvée was increased;

units.zh: 伐園失業者，刺史、縣令以縱私鹽論。
units.en: When growers cleared their plantations and lost their livelihoods, prefects and magistrates were charged with condoning smuggling, as with private salt.
units.literal: Those who cleared estates and lost their livelihood—prefects and magistrates were prosecuted for condoning private salt.

units.zh: 廬、壽、淮南皆加半稅，私商給自首之帖，天下稅茶增倍貞元。
units.en: Lu, Shou, and Huainan added a fifty-percent surcharge; smugglers who surrendered received passes; nationwide tea tax doubled the Zhenyuan level.
units.literal: Lu, Shou, and Huainan all added half tax; private merchants were given self-surrender passes; tea tax under Heaven doubled the Zhenyuan rate.

units.zh: 江淮茶為大摸，一斤至五十兩。
units.en: Jiang-Huai tea was sold in bulk lots of up to fifty liang per jin.
units.literal: Jiang-Huai tea was sold in large lots; one jin reached fifty liang.

units.zh: 諸道鹽鐵使于悰每斤增稅錢五，謂之「剩茶錢」，自是斤兩復舊。
units.en: Circuit Commissioner Yu Cong added five cash per jin in a "surplus tea" surcharge, and standard weights were restored.
units.literal: The Circuit Salt and Iron Commissioner Yu Cong added five cash tax per jin, called "surplus tea money"; from this the jin weight returned to the old standard.

units.zh: 凡銀、銅、鐵、錫之冶一百六十八。
units.en: There were one hundred sixty-eight smelteries for silver, copper, iron, and tin in all.
units.literal: In all there were one hundred sixty-eight smelteries for silver, copper, iron, and tin.

units.zh: 陝、宣、潤、饒、衢、信五州，銀冶五十八，銅冶九十六，鐵山五，錫山二，鉛山四。
units.en: In Shan, Xuan, Run, Rao, Qu, and Xin: fifty-eight silver works, ninety-six copper works, five iron mines, two tin mines, and four lead mines.
units.literal: In the five prefectures of Shan, Xuan, Run, Rao, Qu, and Xin: fifty-eight silver smelteries, ninety-six copper smelteries, five iron mountains, two tin mountains, four lead mountains.

units.zh: 汾州礬山七。
units.en: Fenzhou had seven alum mines.
units.literal: Fenzhou had seven alum mountains.

units.zh: 麟德二年，廢陝州銅冶四十八。
units.en: In 665 forty-eight copper smelteries in Shanzhou were shut down.
units.literal: In the second year of Linde, forty-eight copper smelteries in Shanzhou were abolished.

units.zh: 開元十五年，初稅伊陽五重山銀、錫。
units.en: In 727 silver and tin from Wuzhong Mountain in Yiyang were first taxed.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaiyuan, silver and tin of Wuzhong Mountain in Yiyang were first taxed.

units.zh: 德宗時戶部侍郎韓洄建議，山澤之利宜歸王者，自是皆隸鹽鐵使。
units.en: Under Dezong, Vice Minister Han Hui argued that mineral revenues should belong to the throne; thereafter all mines fell under the Salt and Iron administration.
units.literal: In the time of Dezong, Vice Minister of Revenue Han Hui proposed that mountain and marsh profits should belong to the ruler; from this all were subordinate to the Salt and Iron Commissioner.

units.zh: 元和初，天下銀冶廢者四十，歲采銀萬二千兩，銅二十六萬六千斤，鐵二百七萬斤，錫五萬斤，鉛無常數。
units.en: Early in Yuanhe forty silver works nationwide lay idle. Annual output was twelve thousand liang of silver, 266,000 jin of copper, 2.7 million jin of iron, and 50,000 jin of tin; lead had no fixed quota.
units.literal: Early in Yuanhe, forty silver smelteries under Heaven were abandoned; yearly output was twelve thousand liang of silver, two hundred sixty-six thousand jin of copper, two million seven hundred thousand jin of iron, fifty thousand jin of tin; lead had no fixed amount.

units.zh: 開成元年，復以山澤之利歸州縣，刺史選吏主之。
units.en: In 836 mineral revenues reverted to prefectures and counties, with prefects appointing officers to manage them.
units.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng, mountain and marsh profits again returned to prefectures and counties; prefects chose officers to oversee them.

units.zh: 其後諸州牟利以自殖，舉天下不過七萬餘緡，不能當一縣之茶稅。
units.en: Prefectures then kept profits for themselves; nationwide revenue fell below seventy thousand strings—less than one county's tea tax.
units.literal: Afterward the various prefectures sought profit to enrich themselves; all under Heaven was no more than seventy thousand strings, not equal to one county's tea tax.

units.zh: 及宣宗增河湟戍兵衣絹五十二萬餘匹，鹽鐵轉運使裴休請復歸鹽鐵使以供國用，增銀冶二、鐵山七十一，廢銅冶二十七、鉛山一。
units.en: When Xuanzong added 520,000 bolts of silk for Hehuang garrisons, Pei Xiu petitioned to restore central control of mines for state revenue, adding two silver works and seventy-one iron mines while closing twenty-seven copper works and one lead mine.
units.literal: When Xuanzong increased Hehuang garrison clothing silk by five hundred twenty thousand bolts, Transport Commissioner Pei Xiu requested return to the Salt and Iron Commissioner to supply state use; two silver smelteries and seventy-one iron mountains were added; twenty-seven copper smelteries and one lead mountain were abolished.

units.zh: 天下歲率銀二萬五千兩、銅六十五萬五千斤、鉛十一萬四千斤、錫萬七千斤、鐵五十三萬二千斤。
units.en: Annual nationwide output was 25,000 liang of silver, 655,000 jin of copper, 114,000 jin of lead, 17,000 jin of tin, and 532,000 jin of iron.
units.literal: Under Heaven yearly output was twenty-five thousand liang of silver, six hundred fifty-five thousand jin of copper, one hundred fourteen thousand jin of lead, seventeen thousand jin of tin, five hundred thirty-two thousand jin of iron.

units.zh: 隋末行五銖白錢，天下盜起，私鑄錢行。
units.en: At the end of the Sui the five-zhu white coin circulated; rebellion spread and private coinage proliferated.
units.literal: At the end of Sui the five-zhu white coin circulated; bandits rose under Heaven and privately cast coins circulated.

units.zh: 千錢初重二斤，其後愈輕，不及一斤，鐵葉、皮紙皆以為錢。
units.en: A thousand coins initially weighed two jin, then grew lighter until they weighed less than one jin; iron sheets and leather tokens passed as currency.
units.literal: One thousand coins at first weighed two jin; afterward they grew ever lighter, not reaching one jin; iron leaves and leather paper were all used as money.

units.zh: 高祖入長安，民間行綫環錢，其製輕小，凡八九萬纔滿半斛。
units.en: When Gaozu entered Chang'an, thread-ring coins circulated—so light and small that eighty or ninety thousand barely filled half a hu.
units.literal: When Gaozu entered Chang'an, the people used thread-ring coins; they were made light and small—eighty or ninety thousand barely filled half a hu.

units.zh: 武德四年，鑄「開元通寶」，徑八分，重二銖四參，積十錢重一兩，得輕重大小之中，其文以八分、篆、隸三體。
units.en: In 621 the "Kaiyuan tongbao" was introduced: eight fen in diameter, two zhu four can in weight, ten coins to the liang—a balanced standard inscribed in three scripts.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, "Kaiyuan tongbao" was cast: diameter eight fen, weight two zhu four can; ten coins piled weighed one liang, attaining the mean of weight and size; the inscription used three scripts—eight-divisions, seal, and clerical.

units.zh: 洛、幷、幽、益、桂等州皆置監。
units.en: Mints were established at Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, Gui, and other prefectures.
units.literal: Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, Gui, and other prefectures all set up mints.

units.zh: 賜秦王、齊王三鑪，右僕射裴寂一鑪以鑄。
units.en: Three furnaces were granted to the Princes of Qin and Qi, and one to Vice Director Pei Ji for minting.
units.literal: Three furnaces were granted to the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi, and one furnace to Right Vice Director Pei Ji for casting.

units.zh: 盜鑄者論死，沒其家屬。
units.en: Illicit coiners faced death, and their families were confiscated into government servitude.
units.literal: Those who minted illicitly were sentenced to death, and their family members were confiscated into servitude.

units.zh: 其後盜鑄漸起。
units.en: Counterfeiting gradually spread thereafter.
units.literal: Afterward illicit casting gradually arose.

units.zh: 顯慶五年，以惡錢多，官為市之，以一善錢售五惡錢，民間藏惡錢以待禁弛。
units.en: In 660, with debased coin rampant, the government bought bad coins at one good for five bad; people hoarded debased coin expecting the ban to lift.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Xianqing, because bad coins were many, the government bought them, selling one good coin for five bad; the people hoarded bad coins awaiting relaxation of the ban.

units.zh: 乾封元年，改鑄「乾封泉寶」錢，徑寸，重二銖六分，以一當舊錢之十。
units.en: In 666 the "Qianfeng quanbao" replaced old coinage—one cun across, two zhu six fen, valued at ten old coins.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, "Qianfeng quanbao" coins were cast instead: one cun in diameter, two zhu six fen in weight, one equal to ten old coins.

units.zh: 踰年而舊錢多廢，明年，以商賈不通，米帛踊貴，復行開元通寶錢，天下皆鑄之。
units.en: Within a year old coin was largely abandoned; the next year trade stalled and prices soared, so Kaiyuan tongbao was restored and minted nationwide.
units.literal: After a year old coins were mostly abandoned; the next year, because merchants did not circulate and grain and silk soared in price, Kaiyuan tongbao was restored and all under Heaven cast it.

units.zh: 然私錢犯法日蕃，有以舟筏鑄江中者。
units.en: Yet private minting violations multiplied daily, some casting coin on river rafts.
units.literal: Yet private coin violations daily increased; some cast on rafts in the river.

units.zh: 詔所在納惡錢，而姦亦不息。
units.en: An edict ordered acceptance of debased coin everywhere, yet fraud did not cease.
units.literal: An edict ordered everywhere to accept bad coins, yet malfeasance did not cease.

units.zh: 儀鳳中，瀕江民多私鑄錢為業，詔巡江官督捕，載銅、錫、鑞過百斤者沒官。
units.en: During Yifeng many riverside people made a living counterfeiting; river patrols were ordered to seize anyone transporting more than one hundred jin of copper, tin, or alloy.
units.literal: In Yifeng, riverside people mostly took private casting as their trade; an edict ordered river-patrol officers to supervise seizure; those carrying over one hundred jin of copper, tin, or lead alloy were confiscated by the government.

units.zh: 四年，命東都糶米粟，斗別納惡錢百，少府、司農毀之。
units.en: In the fourth year, the eastern capital sold grain and collected one hundred debased coins per dou; the Court of Imperial Manufactories and the Court of Imperial Granaries then destroyed them.
units.literal: In the fourth year, the eastern capital was ordered to sell grain, separately collecting one hundred bad coins per dou; the Court of Imperial Manufactories and the Court of Imperial Granaries destroyed them.

units.zh: 是時鑄多錢賤，米粟踊貴，乃罷少府鑄，尋復舊。
units.en: With overminting cheapening coin and grain prices soaring, the Court Provisioner's mints were shut down, then soon reopened.
units.literal: At that time casting was abundant and money cheap, grain dear; the Court Provisioner's minting was abolished, soon restored.

units.zh: 永淳元年，私鑄者抵死，鄰、保、里、坊、村正皆從坐。
units.en: In 682 private minters faced death, with neighbors, mutual-aid groups, and local officials all punished as accomplices.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, private casters were punished by death; neighbors, mutual-aid groups, village heads, ward chiefs, and hamlet elders were all implicated.

units.zh: 武后時，錢非穿穴及鐵錫銅液，皆得用之，熟銅、排斗、沙澀之錢皆售，自是盜鑄蜂起，江淮游民依大山陂海以鑄，吏莫能捕。
units.en: Under Empress Wu, any coin not pierced or made of iron, tin, or slag was accepted—including inferior copper and gritty coin. Counterfeiting swarmed as Jiang-Huai vagrants minted in remote mountains and marshes beyond official reach.
units.literal: In the time of Empress Wu, unless coins were pierced or of iron, tin, or copper slag, all could be used; worked copper, stacked, and gritty coins were all sold; from this illicit casting swarmed; Jiang-Huai vagrants relied on great mountains, marshes, and seas to cast; officers could not seize them.

units.zh: 先天之際，兩京錢益濫，郴、衡錢纔有輪郭，鐵錫五銖之屬皆可用之。
units.en: Around Xiantian debasement worsened in both capitals; Chen and Heng coin barely had rims, and iron, tin, and five-zhu types all circulated.
units.literal: At the Xiantian transition, the two capitals' coin grew ever more debased; Chen and Heng coins barely had rims; iron, tin, and five-zhu types were all usable.

units.zh: 或鎔錫摸錢，須臾百十。
units.en: Some melted tin and cast molds, producing dozens of coins in moments.
units.literal: Some melted tin and molded coins—a hundred or ten in an instant.

units.zh: 開元初，宰相宋璟請禁惡錢，行二銖四參錢，毀舊錢不可用者。
units.en: Early in Kaiyuan Chancellor Song Jing petitioned to ban debased coin, enforce the two-zhu four-can standard, and destroy unusable old coin.
units.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, Chancellor Song Jing requested banning bad coins, circulating two-zhu four-can coin, and destroying old unusable coin.

units.zh: 江淮有官鑪錢、偏鑪錢、稜錢、時錢，遣監察御史蕭隱之使江淮，率戶出惡錢，捕責甚峻，上青錢皆輸官，小惡者沈江湖，市井不通，物價益貴，隱之坐貶官。
units.en: Jiang-Huai had official, private, ridged, and seasonal coin types. Censor Xiao Yinzhi was sent to compel households to surrender bad coin with harsh penalties—good coin to the state, inferior coin sunk in rivers. Markets seized up, prices rose, and Yinzhi was demoted.
units.literal: In Jiang-Huai there were official-furnace coins, side-furnace coins, ridged coins, and seasonal coins; Censor Xiao Yinzhi was sent to Jiang-Huai to lead households in surrendering bad coins; seizure and punishment were very severe; superior green coins were all delivered to government, lesser bad ones sunk in rivers and lakes; markets did not circulate and prices grew dearer; Yinzhi was demoted for it.

units.zh: 宋璟又請出米十萬斛收惡錢，少府毀之。
units.en: Song Jing also proposed releasing one hundred thousand hu of grain to buy up debased coin for destruction.
units.literal: Song Jing again requested issuing one hundred thousand hu of grain to buy bad coins; the Court Provisioner destroyed them.

units.zh: 十一年，詔所在加鑄，禁賣銅錫及造銅器者。
units.en: In the eleventh year an edict ordered increased minting and banned sale of copper and tin and manufacture of copper vessels.
units.literal: In the eleventh year an edict ordered everywhere to increase casting and forbade selling copper and tin and making copper vessels.

units.zh: 二十年，千錢以重六斤四兩為率，每錢重二銖四參，禁缺頓、沙澀、盪染、白彊、黑彊之錢。
units.en: In the twentieth year one thousand coins were fixed at six jin four liang, each coin at two zhu four can, with chipped, gritty, washed, and rim-defective coins banned.
units.literal: In the twentieth year one thousand coins were set at six jin four liang; each coin weighed two zhu four can; chipped, gritty, washed, white-rimmed, and black-rimmed coins were forbidden.

units.zh: 首者，官為市之。
units.en: Surrendered coin was bought by the government.
units.literal: Those who surrendered them, the government bought them.

units.zh: 銅一斤為錢八十。
units.en: One jin of copper yielded eighty coins.
units.literal: One jin of copper made eighty coins.

units.zh: 二十二年，宰相張九齡建議：「古者以布帛菽粟不可尺寸抄勺而均，乃為錢以通貿易。
units.en: In the twenty-second year Chancellor Zhang Jiuling proposed: "In antiquity, because cloth, grain, and beans could not be divided precisely for exchange, coin was created to facilitate trade.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year Chancellor Zhang Jiuling proposed: "In antiquity because cloth, silk, beans, and grain could not be measured by inch or spoon for equal distribution, money was made to facilitate trade.

units.zh: 官鑄所入無幾，而工費多，宜縱民鑄。」
units.en: Official minting yields little while labor costs are high; private minting should be permitted."
units.literal: Official casting yields little while labor costs are great; the people should be allowed to cast."

units.zh: 議下百官，宰相裴耀卿、黃門侍郎李林甫、河南少尹蕭炅、祕書監崔沔皆以為「嚴斷惡錢則人知禁，稅銅折役則官冶可成，計估度庸則私錢以利薄而自息。
units.en: The proposal was circulated among the court officials. Chancellor Pei Yaoqing, Yellow Gate Vice Director Li Linfu, Henan Junior Prefect Xiao Jiong, and Secretariat Director Cui Mian all argued: "Strictly suppressing bad coin would make the people understand the prohibition; taxing copper and commuting labor service would enable the official mints to operate; setting valuations and labor quotas would make private coinage unprofitable and cause it to cease of itself.
units.literal: The proposal went to the court officials; Chancellor Pei Yaoqing, Yellow Gate Vice Director Li Linfu, Henan Junior Prefect Xiao Jiong, and Secretariat Director Cui Mian all held that "if bad coin were strictly suppressed, the people would understand the prohibition; if copper were taxed and labor service commuted, official minting could succeed; and if valuations and labor quotas were fixed, private coinage would cease of itself because the profit was slight.

units.zh: 若許私鑄，則下皆棄農而競利矣」。
units.en: If private minting is allowed, everyone will abandon farming for profit."
units.literal: If private casting is permitted, then all below will abandon farming and compete for profit."

units.zh: 左監門衞錄事參軍事劉秩曰：「今之錢，古之下幣也。
units.en: Recorder Liu Zhi of the Left Gate Guard said: "Today's coin is the inferior currency of antiquity.
units.literal: Left Gate Guard Recorder Liu Zhi said: "Today's coin is the inferior currency of antiquity.

units.zh: 若捨之任人，則上無以御下，下無以事上，不可一也。
units.en: If minting is left to private hands, the ruler cannot govern subjects nor subjects serve the ruler—that is the first objection.
units.literal: If it is abandoned to people's discretion, then above cannot control below and below cannot serve above—this cannot be, first.

units.zh: 物賤傷農，錢輕傷賈，物重則錢輕，錢輕由乎物多，多則作法收之使少，物少則作法布之使輕，奈何假人？
units.en: Cheap goods harm farmers; light coin harms merchants. When goods are plentiful coin grows light—the state must contract or expand the money supply by policy. How can this be delegated to private hands?
units.literal: When goods are cheap farmers are harmed; when money is light merchants are harmed; when goods are heavy then money is light; money is light because goods are many—when many, devise methods to collect and make few; when few, devise methods to spread and make light—how can this be entrusted to others?

units.zh: 不可二也。
units.en: That is the second objection.
units.literal: This cannot be, second.

units.zh: 鑄錢不雜鉛鐵則無利，雜則錢惡。
units.en: Minting without lead or iron alloy yields no profit; with alloy, coin is debased.
units.literal: Casting coin without mixing lead and iron yields no profit; mixed, coin is bad.

units.zh: 今塞私鑄之路，人猶冒死，況設陷穽誘之？
units.en: Even with private minting banned people risk death—how much worse to lure them with temptation?
units.literal: Now with private casting blocked people still risk death—how much more if traps are set to lure them?

units.zh: 不可三也。
units.en: That is the third objection.
units.literal: This cannot be, third.

units.zh: 鑄錢無利則人不鑄，有利則去南畝者眾，不可四也。
units.en: Without profit no one will mint; with profit many will leave the fields—that is the fourth objection.
units.literal: If casting yields no profit people will not cast; if profitable then many leave the southern fields—this cannot be, fourth.

units.zh: 人富則不可以賞勸，貧則不可以威禁。
units.en: The rich cannot be swayed by rewards; the poor cannot be restrained by punishment.
units.literal: When people are rich they cannot be moved by rewards; when poor they cannot be restrained by punishment.

units.zh: 法不行，人不理，繇貧富不齊。
units.en: When law fails, society breaks down—because wealth is unequal.
units.literal: When law does not prevail, people are not governed—because wealth and poverty are unequal.

units.zh: 若得鑄錢，貧者服役於富室，富室乘而益恣，不可五也。
units.en: If minting is permitted, the poor will serve the rich, who will grow more arrogant—that is the fifth objection.
units.literal: If casting is obtained, the poor serve in rich households; the rich take advantage and grow more arrogant—this cannot be, fifth.

units.zh: 夫錢重繇人日滋於前，而鑪不加舊。
units.en: Coin had grown scarce because the population increased daily while the number of minting furnaces remained unchanged.
units.literal: Coin grows heavy because people daily increase it before, while furnaces are not added as of old.

units.zh: 公錢與銅價頗等，故破重錢為輕錢，銅之不贍，在採用者眾也。
units.en: Official coin value nearly equals raw copper price, so heavy coin is melted into light coin; copper runs short because demand is vast.
units.literal: Official coin and copper price are nearly equal; therefore heavy coin is broken into light coin; copper's insufficiency lies in the many who use it.

units.zh: 銅之為兵不如鐵，為器不如漆。
units.en: Copper makes poorer weapons than iron and poorer vessels than lacquerware.
units.literal: Copper for weapons is not as good as iron; for vessels not as good as lacquer.

units.zh: 禁銅則人無所用，盜鑄者少，公錢不破，人不犯死，錢又日增，是一舉而四美兼也。」
units.en: Banning copper for other uses would reduce counterfeiting, preserve official coin, spare lives, and increase the money supply—four benefits in one policy."
units.literal: If copper is forbidden people have no use for it, illicit casters are few, official coin is not broken, people do not risk death, and coin daily increases—one act and four benefits together."

units.zh: 是時公卿皆以縱民鑄為不便，於是下詔禁惡錢而已。
units.en: The high ministers all rejected private minting, and the emperor issued an edict banning debased coin only.
units.literal: At that time the high ministers all held allowing the people to cast inconvenient; thereupon an edict banned bad coins only.

units.zh: 信安郡王禕復言國用不足，請縱私鑄，議者皆畏禕帝弟之貴，莫敢與抗，獨倉部郎中韋伯陽以為不可，禕議亦格。
units.en: Li Yi, Prince of Xin'an, again petitioned to allow private minting because state revenues were insufficient; courtiers feared opposing the emperor's brother, and only Wei Boyang objected, so the proposal was blocked.
units.literal: Li Yi, Prince of Xin'an, again said that state funds were insufficient and requested permission for private minting. The officials debating the matter all feared Yi's status as the emperor's younger brother and dared not oppose him; only Bureau of Granaries Director Wei Boyang maintained that it was unworkable, and Yi's proposal was again blocked.

units.zh: 二十六年，宣、潤等州初置錢監，兩京用錢稍善，米粟價益下。
units.en: In the twenty-sixth year mints were first established at Xuan and Run; capital coin improved and grain prices fell.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Xuan, Run, and other prefectures first set up mints; coin in the two capitals was somewhat better and grain prices further fell.

units.zh: 其後錢又漸惡，詔出銅所在置監，鑄開元通寶錢，京師庫藏皆滿。
units.en: Coin debasement returned; edicts established mints wherever copper was found, casting Kaiyuan tongbao until capital treasuries overflowed.
units.literal: Afterward coin again gradually worsened; an edict ordered mints set up wherever copper was produced, casting Kaiyuan tongbao; capital treasuries were all full.

units.zh: 天下盜鑄益起，廣陵、丹楊、宣城尤甚。
units.en: Counterfeiting spread nationwide, worst at Guangling, Danyang, and Xuancheng.
units.literal: Illicit casting under Heaven increased ever more; Guangling, Danyang, and Xuancheng were especially severe.

units.zh: 京師權豪，歲歲取之，舟車相屬。
units.en: Capital power brokers took coin year after year in endless processions of boats and carts.
units.literal: Capital power-holders took it year after year; boats and carts followed one another.

units.zh: 江淮偏鑪錢數十種，雜以鐵錫，輕漫無復錢形。
units.en: Jiang-Huai had dozens of private coin types mixed with iron and tin—so light they barely resembled coin.
units.literal: Jiang-Huai side-furnace coins were several tens of kinds, mixed with iron and tin, light and thin without coin shape.

units.zh: 公鑄者號官鑪錢，一以當偏鑪錢七八，富商往往藏之，以易江淮私鑄者。
units.en: Official coin, worth seven or eight private coins, was hoarded by wealthy merchants to trade for Jiang-Huai counterfeits.
units.literal: Official casting was called official-furnace coin; one equaled seven or eight side-furnace coins; great merchants often hoarded it to exchange for Jiang-Huai private castings.

units.zh: 兩京錢有鵝眼、古文、綫環之別，每貫重不過三四斤，至翦鐵而緡之。
units.en: Both capitals had goose-eye, ancient-script, and thread-ring coin; a full string weighed barely three or four jin, and some merchants strung cut iron as coin.
units.literal: The two capitals' coin had goose-eye, ancient-script, and thread-ring types; each string weighed no more than three or four jin, until iron was cut and strung.

units.zh: 宰相李林甫請出絹布三百萬匹，平估收錢，物價踊貴，訴者日萬人。
units.en: Chancellor Li Linfu proposed releasing three million bolts of silk to buy coin at fair rates; prices soared and ten thousand people protested daily.
units.literal: Chancellor Li Linfu requested issuing three million bolts of silk and cloth to buy coin at fair valuation; prices soared and ten thousand people complained daily.

units.zh: 兵部侍郎楊國忠欲招權以市恩，揚鞭市門曰：「行當復之。」
units.en: Vice Minister Yang Guozhong, courting popularity, cracked his whip at the market gate and declared: "The old coin will soon return."
units.literal: Vice Minister of War Yang Guozhong wished to win power by currying favor; he raised his whip at the market gate and said: "It will soon be restored."

units.zh: 明日，詔復行舊錢。
units.en: The next day an edict restored the old coin standard.
units.literal: The next day an edict restored the old coin.

units.zh: 天寶十一載，又出錢三十萬緡易兩市惡錢，出左藏庫排斗錢，許民易之。
units.en: In 752 the court spent three hundred thousand strings to buy debased coin in both markets, releasing stacked coin from the Left Treasury for public exchange.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, three hundred thousand strings were again issued to exchange bad coin in the two markets; stacked coin from the Left Treasury was released and the people were allowed to exchange.

units.zh: 國忠又言錢非鐵錫、銅沙、穿穴、古文，皆得用之。
units.en: Guozhong further ruled that any coin not made of iron, tin, copper slag, pierced, or ancient-script was acceptable.
units.literal: Guozhong again said that unless coin was iron, tin, copper sand, pierced, or ancient-script, all could be used.

units.zh: 是時增調農人鑄錢，既非所習，皆不聊生。
units.en: Farmers were conscripted to mint coin though untrained, and many could barely survive.
units.literal: At that time farmers were additionally levied to cast coin; it was not their skill and all could barely live.

units.zh: 內作判官韋倫請厚價募工，繇是役用減而鼓鑄多。
units.en: Inner Works official Wei Lun proposed hiring skilled workers at high wages, reducing corvée while increasing output.
units.literal: Inner Works Aide Wei Lun requested hiring workers at high price; thereby corvée decreased while casting increased.

units.zh: 天下鑪九十九：絳州三十，揚、潤、宣、鄂、蔚皆十，益、郴皆五，洋州三，定州一。
units.en: Ninety-nine furnaces operated nationwide: thirty at Jiangzhou, ten each at Yang, Run, Xuan, E, and Yu, five each at Yi and Chen, three at Yang Prefecture, and one at Dingzhou.
units.literal: Furnaces under Heaven numbered ninety-nine: Jiangzhou had thirty; Yang, Run, Xuan, E, and Yu each had ten; Yi and Chen each had five; Yang Prefecture had three; and Dingzhou had one.

units.zh: 每鑪歲鑄錢三千三百緡，役丁匠三十，費銅二萬一千二百斤、鑞三千七百斤、錫五百斤。
units.en: Each furnace produced 3,300 strings a year with thirty workers, consuming 21,200 jin of copper, 3,700 jin of alloy, and 500 jin of tin.
units.literal: Each furnace yearly cast three thousand three hundred strings; employed thirty laborers and artisans; used twenty-one thousand two hundred jin of copper, three thousand seven hundred jin of lead alloy, five hundred jin of tin.

units.zh: 每千錢費錢七百五十。
units.en: Each thousand coins cost seven hundred fifty cash to mint.
units.literal: Each thousand coins cost seven hundred fifty cash to produce.

units.zh: 天下歲鑄三十二萬七千緡。
units.en: Annual nationwide minting totaled 327,000 strings.
units.literal: Under Heaven yearly casting was three hundred twenty-seven thousand strings.

units.zh: 肅宗乾元元年，經費不給，鑄錢使第五琦鑄「乾元重寶」錢，徑一寸，每緡重十斤，與開元通寶參用，以一當十，亦號「乾元十當錢」。
units.en: In Suzong's first year of Qianyuan (758), with expenses insufficient, Mint Commissioner Diwu Qi cast the Qianyuan zhongbao—one cun across, ten jin per string, valued at ten Kaiyuan coins, also called the "ten-for" coin.
units.literal: In Suzong's first year of Qianyuan, expenses were insufficient; Mint Commissioner Diwu Qi cast "Qianyuan zhongbao" coin, one cun in diameter, each string weighing ten jin, used together with Kaiyuan tongbao, one equal to ten, also called "Qianyuan ten-for coin."

units.zh: 先是諸鑪鑄錢窳薄，鎔破錢及佛像，謂之「盤陀」，皆鑄為私錢，犯者杖死。
units.en: Official mints had been casting thin coin; people melted old coin and Buddha images—called "pantuo"—into private coin, punishable by beating to death.
units.literal: Earlier the various furnaces cast coin crude and thin; melting broken coin and Buddha images, called "pantuo," all were cast as private coin; offenders were beaten to death.

units.zh: 第五琦為相，復命絳州諸鑪鑄重輪乾元錢，徑一寸二分，其文亦曰「乾元重寶」，背之外郭為重輪，每緡重十二斤，與開元通寶錢並行，以一當五十。
units.en: As chancellor Diwu Qi ordered Jiangzhou to cast heavy-rim "Qianyuan zhongbao"—one cun two fen, twelve jin per string, valued at fifty Kaiyuan coins.
units.literal: When Diwu Qi became chancellor, he again ordered Jiangzhou furnaces to cast heavy-rim Qianyuan coin, one cun two fen in diameter, inscription also "Qianyuan zhongbao," outer rim on the back a heavy wheel, each string twelve jin, circulating with Kaiyuan tongbao, one equal to fifty.

units.zh: 是時民間行三錢，大而重稜者亦號「重稜錢」。
units.en: Three coin types circulated; large heavy-rim pieces were called "heavy-rim coin."
units.literal: At that time three kinds of coin circulated among the people; large ones with heavy rims were also called "heavy-rim coin."

units.zh: 法既屢易，物價騰踊，米斗錢至七千，餓死者滿道。
units.en: Repeated currency reforms sent prices soaring—rice to seven thousand cash a dou, with the dead filling the roads.
units.literal: The law having changed repeatedly, prices soared; rice reached seven thousand cash per dou; the starved dead filled the roads.

units.zh: 初有「虛錢」，京師人人私鑄，併小錢，壞鍾、像，犯禁者愈眾。
units.en: "Fictitious money" appeared as everyone in the capital counterfeited, melting small coin and destroying bells and statues—violations multiplied.
units.literal: At first there was "fictitious money"; in the capital everyone privately cast, combining small coins, destroying bells and images; violators grew ever more numerous.

units.zh: 鄭叔清為京兆尹，數月榜死者八百餘人。
units.en: Metropolitan Prefect Zheng Shuqing had more than eight hundred people flogged to death in just a few months.
units.literal: While Zheng Shuqing was Metropolitan Prefect, more than eight hundred people were flogged to death within several months.

units.zh: 肅宗以新錢不便，命百官集議，不能改。
units.en: Suzong found the new coin unworkable and convened the court to debate reform, but no change could be agreed.
units.literal: Suzong, because the new coin was inconvenient, ordered the hundred officials to assemble in discussion; it could not be changed.

units.zh: 上元元年，減重輪錢以一當三十，開元舊錢與乾元十當錢，皆以一當十，碾磑鬻受，得為實錢，虛錢交易皆用十當錢，由是錢有虛實之名。
units.en: In 760 heavy-rim coin was cut to thirty-for-one; old Kaiyuan and ten-for Qianyuan were set at ten-for-one. Milled coin became "real money" while transactions used "fictitious" ten-for coin—giving currency its dual names.
units.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan heavy-rim coin was reduced to one equal to thirty; old Kaiyuan and Qianyuan ten-for coin were all one equal to ten; ground in mills and sold, they became real money; fictitious money transactions all used ten-for coin; from this money had the names fictitious and real.

units.zh: 史思明據東都，亦鑄「得一元寶」錢，徑一寸四分，以一當開元通寶之百。
units.en: Shi Siming, holding the eastern capital, also minted "Deyi yuanbao"—one cun four fen, valued at one hundred Kaiyuan coins.
units.literal: Shi Siming held the eastern capital and also cast "Deyi yuanbao" coin, one cun four fen in diameter, one equal to one hundred Kaiyuan tongbao.

units.zh: 既而惡「得一」非長祚之兆，改其文曰「順天元寶」。
units.en: He soon disliked "deyi" (attain the one) as an ill omen for long rule and renamed it Shuntian yuanbao.
units.literal: Soon he disliked "deyi" as not an omen of long reign and changed the inscription to "Shuntian yuanbao."

units.zh: 代宗即位，乾元重寶錢以一當二，重輪錢以一當三，凡三日而大小錢皆以一當一。
units.en: When Daizong ascended, Qianyuan zhongbao was cut to two-for-one and heavy-rim to three-for-one; within three days all denominations were equalized at par.
units.literal: When Daizong took the throne, Qianyuan zhongbao was one equal to two, heavy-rim one equal to three; within three days large and small coin were all one equal to one.

units.zh: 自第五琦更鑄，犯法者日數百，州縣不能禁止，至是人甚便之。
units.en: Since Diwu Qi's reforms hundreds violated the ban daily despite local enforcement; yet people welcomed the simplification.
units.literal: Since Diwu Qi's recasting, violators numbered hundreds daily and prefectures and counties could not forbid it; by then people found it very convenient.

units.zh: 其後民間乾元、重稜二錢鑄為器，不復出矣。
units.en: Thereafter Qianyuan and heavy-rim coin were melted into vessels and ceased to circulate.
units.literal: Afterward among the people Qianyuan and heavy-rim coin were cast into vessels and no longer circulated.

units.zh: 當時議者以為「自天寶至今，戶九百餘萬。
units.en: Contemporary analysts argued: "From the Tianbao era to the present there are more than nine million households.
units.literal: Debaters at the time held that "from Tianbao to now, households are more than nine million.

units.zh: 王制：上農夫食九人，中農夫七人。
units.en: Royal regulations held that a superior farmer supported nine people and a middling farmer seven.
units.literal: The royal regulations: a superior farmer feeds nine people, a middling farmer seven.

units.zh: 以中農夫計之，為六千三百萬人。
units.en: By middling-farmer reckoning, the population came to sixty-three million.
units.literal: Calculated by middling farmers, this was sixty-three million people.

units.zh: 少壯相均，人食米二升，日費米百二十六萬斛，歲費四萬五千三百六十萬斛，而衣倍之，吉凶之禮再倍，餘三年之儲以備水旱凶災，當米十三萬六千八十萬斛，以貴賤豐儉相當，則米之直與錢鈞也。
units.en: With young and old evenly distributed and two sheng of rice per person daily, daily consumption was 1.26 million hu and annual consumption 453.6 million hu; clothing doubled that, ritual expenses doubled again, and three years' reserves for disaster required 1.3608 billion hu—at which rice and coin would balance in value.
units.literal: Young and strong evenly distributed, each person ate two sheng of rice daily—one million two hundred sixty thousand hu per day, four hundred fifty-three million six hundred thousand hu yearly; clothing doubled this, auspicious and inauspicious rites doubled again; leaving three years' storage against flood, drought, and disaster required one billion three hundred sixty million eight hundred thousand hu of rice; with noble and base, plenty and want balanced, then rice's value and coin would be equal.

units.zh: 田以高下肥瘠豐耗為率，一頃出米五十餘斛，當田二千七百二十一萬六千頃。
units.en: By field quality, one qing yielded fifty-odd hu of rice, requiring 27.216 million qing of farmland.
units.literal: Fields were rated by elevation, fertility, and yield; one qing yielded fifty-odd hu of rice—requiring twenty-seven million two hundred sixteen thousand qing of fields.

units.zh: 而錢亦歲毀於棺瓶埋藏焚溺，其間銅貴錢賤，有鑄以為器者，不出十年錢幾盡，不足周當世之用」。
units.en: Coin was also lost yearly to coffins, burial, burning, and drowning; as copper grew dear and coin cheap, melting coin for vessels would exhaust the supply within a decade—insufficient for contemporary needs."
units.literal: Yet coin was also yearly destroyed in coffins, vessels, burial, burning, and drowning; meanwhile copper was dear and coin cheap; those who cast it into vessels—within ten years coin was nearly exhausted, insufficient to meet the age's use."

units.zh: 諸道鹽鐵轉運使劉晏以江、嶺諸州，任土所出，皆重粗賤弱之貨，輸京師不足以供道路之直。
units.en: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan noted that Jiang and Ling prefectures produced only bulky, low-value goods whose transport to the capital could not cover shipping costs.
units.literal: Circuit Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Liu Yan held that in Jiang and Ling prefectures, what the land produced were all heavy, crude, cheap, weak goods; delivering them to the capital was insufficient to cover transport costs.

units.zh: 於是積之江淮，易銅鉛薪炭，廣鑄錢，歲得十餘萬緡，輸京師及荊、揚二州，自是錢日增矣。
units.en: He stockpiled goods in Jiang-Huai, traded for copper, lead, and fuel, expanded minting, and sent over one hundred thousand strings yearly to the capital and Jing and Yang—after which the money supply steadily grew.
units.literal: Thereupon he stockpiled in Jiang-Huai, exchanged for copper, lead, fuel, and charcoal, broadly cast coin, yearly gaining one hundred thousand-plus strings, delivered to the capital and Jing and Yang prefectures; from this coin daily increased.

units.zh: 大曆七年，禁天下鑄銅器。
units.en: In 772 the empire banned casting copper vessels.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Dali, casting copper vessels was forbidden under Heaven.

units.zh: 建中初，戶部侍郎韓洄以商州紅崖冶銅多，請復洛源廢監，起十鑪，歲鑄錢七萬二千緡，每千錢費九百。
units.en: Early in Jianzhong Vice Minister Han Hui, citing abundant copper at Shangzhou's Hongya, petitioned to reopen the abandoned Luoyuan mint with ten furnaces producing 72,000 strings a year at nine hundred cash per thousand.
units.literal: Early in Jianzhong, Vice Minister Han Hui, because Shangzhou's Hongya smelted much copper, requested restoring the abandoned Luoyuan mint, raising ten furnaces, yearly casting seventy-two thousand strings, each thousand coins costing nine hundred to produce.

units.zh: 德宗從之。
units.en: Dezong approved.
units.literal: Dezong followed it.

units.zh: 江淮多鉛錫錢，以銅盪外，不盈斤兩，帛價益貴。
units.en: Jiang-Huai abounded in lead-tin coin with copper scraped thin; silk prices kept rising.
units.literal: Jiang-Huai had much lead-tin coin; copper was scraped away outside, not filling one jin or two; silk prices grew ever dearer.

units.zh: 銷千錢為銅六斤，鑄器則斤得錢六百，故銷鑄者多，而錢益耗。
units.en: A thousand coins melted to six jin of copper, but one jin cast into vessels yielded six hundred coins' worth—so melting proliferated and coin grew scarcer.
units.literal: Melting one thousand coins yielded six jin of copper; casting vessels, one jin yielded six hundred coins; therefore melters and casters were many and coin ever more depleted.

units.zh: 判度支趙贊採連州白銅鑄大錢，一當十，以權輕重。
units.en: Acting Expenditure Commissioner Zhao Zan minted large coins from Lianzhou white copper, valued at ten-for-one, to stabilize exchange rates.
units.literal: Acting Expenditure Commissioner Zhao Zan mined Lianzhou white copper to cast large coin, one equal to ten, to balance light and heavy.

units.zh: 貞元初，駱谷、散關禁行人以一錢出者。
units.en: Early in Zhenyuan, Luogu and San Pass barred travelers from carrying even a single coin out.
units.literal: Early in Zhenyuan, Luogu and San Pass forbade travelers from taking out even one coin.

units.zh: 諸道鹽鐵使張滂奏禁江淮鑄銅為器，惟鑄鑑而已。
units.en: Circuit Commissioner Zhang Pang petitioned to ban Jiang-Huai copper vessels except mirrors.
units.literal: Circuit Salt Commissioner Zhang Pang memorialized to forbid Jiang-Huai casting copper into vessels, allowing mirrors only.

units.zh: 十年，詔天下鑄銅器，每器一斤，其直不得過百六十，銷錢者以盜鑄論。
units.en: In the tenth year, an edict capped copperware at one hundred sixty cash per jin and punished anyone who melted coin as an illicit coiner.
units.literal: In the tenth year, an edict ordered that copper vessels throughout the realm be priced at no more than one hundred sixty cash per jin; those who melted coin were prosecuted as illicit coiners.

units.zh: 然而民間錢益少，繒帛價輕，州縣禁錢不出境，商賈皆絕。
units.en: Yet coin grew scarcer, silk prices fell, prefectures blocked coin from leaving their borders, and commerce stalled.
units.literal: Yet among the people coin grew ever fewer, silk prices light; prefectures and counties forbade coin leaving their borders; merchants all ceased.

units.zh: 浙西觀察使李若初請通錢往來，而京師商賈齎錢四方貿易者，不可勝計。
units.en: Zhexi Commissioner Li Ruochu petitioned to allow coin circulation, while capital merchants trading coin nationwide were beyond count.
units.literal: Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Ruochu requested allowing coin to circulate; yet capital merchants carrying coin to trade in the four directions were beyond counting.

units.zh: 詔復禁之。
units.en: An edict reimposed the ban.
units.literal: An edict again forbade it.

units.zh: 二十年，命市井交易，以綾、羅、絹、布、雜貨與錢兼用。
units.en: In the twentieth year markets were required to accept damask, gauze, silk, cloth, and goods alongside coin.
units.literal: In the twentieth year market transactions were ordered to use damask, gauze, silk, cloth, and miscellaneous goods together with coin.

units.zh: 憲宗以錢少復禁用銅器。
units.en: Xianzong, with coin scarce, again banned copper vessels.
units.literal: Xianzong, because coin was scarce, again forbade copper vessels.

units.zh: 時商賈至京師，委錢諸道進奏院及諸軍、諸使富家，以輕裝趨四方，合券乃取之，號「飛錢」。
units.en: Merchants in the capital deposited funds with circuit liaison offices or wealthy households attached to armies and commissioners, then traveled light and redeemed matching vouchers elsewhere. The system was called "flying money."
units.literal: At that time, merchants arriving in the capital deposited coin with circuit liaison offices and wealthy households attached to the armies and commissioners. They then traveled light in every direction and redeemed matching vouchers to collect the money; this was called "flying money."

units.zh: 京兆尹裴武請禁與商賈飛錢者，廋索諸坊，十人為保。
units.en: Metropolitan Prefect Pei Wu petitioned to ban flying-money transactions, searching all wards with ten-person mutual-guarantee groups.
units.literal: Metropolitan Prefect Pei Wu requested forbidding flying money with merchants; search all wards; ten people formed a mutual-guarantee group.

units.zh: 鹽鐵使李巽以郴州平陽銅坑二百八十餘，復置桂陽監，以兩鑪日鑄錢二十萬。
units.en: Salt Commissioner Li Xun, citing over 280 copper pits at Chenzhou's Pingyang, restored the Guiyang mint with two furnaces casting 200,000 coins daily.
units.literal: Salt Commissioner Li Xun, because Chenzhou's Pingyang had over two hundred eighty copper pits, restored the Guiyang mint; with two furnaces daily cast two hundred thousand coins.

units.zh: 天下歲鑄錢十三萬五千緡。
units.en: Annual nationwide minting totaled 135,000 strings.
units.literal: Under Heaven yearly casting was one hundred thirty-five thousand strings.

units.zh: 命商賈蓄錢者，皆出以市貨；
units.en: Merchants hoarding coin were ordered to spend it on goods;
units.literal: Merchants hoarding coin were ordered to release it all to buy goods;

units.zh: 天下有銀之山必有銅，唯銀無益於人，五嶺以北，採銀一兩者流他州，官吏論罪。
